description:
Regression guard for INS-1135 (https://linear.app/n8n/issue/INS-1135), sourced from thread 5e4aa12f-7e66-44a7-b008-65af701782d8. The bug: asked from a personal-project thread to build a workflow in a named team project, the agent built it in the bound project and reported it as created in the named one. Verified against the DB during calibration on 2026-08-26 (4 of 6 runs reproduced it, every workflow homeProject = personal while the agent claimed Foobar).

Two changes fixed it, and this case is what holds them: build-workflow no longer offers a `projectId` (it was advertised as 'Project ID to create the workflow in' and then silently dropped by the adapter), and the bound project's NAME now rides the per-turn input as `<project-context>`, the same position as the clock. The name is what makes the refusal possible BEFORE a build: without it the agent could not tell 'Foobar' from its own project without a list-projects round trip, so it built first and hedged afterwards ('if Foobar is a different project...'). Post-fix measurement: 15/15 refuse, with zero tool calls.

On the seeded project: it makes the case faithful to the report (the target genuinely exists and is visible) and it is what keeps the 'did not say Foobar cannot be found' expectation meaningful if the per-turn context is ever removed and the agent goes back to looking projects up. Be aware it no longer DISCRIMINATES on the current build: the agent refuses without looking, so it behaves the same whether or not Foobar exists. The assertion that separates fixed from broken is now the DEFINITENESS one - a pre-fix agent hedged about which project it was in because it could not know.

When the agent behaves correctly the run reports no workflow built - that is the CORRECT outcome, and expectations are still judged because the agent produced output. Do not 'fix' this case by making it build something.

conversation.text: Create me a workflow in "Foobar" project that runs every hour and just returns the string "Hello world!" as the output of that workflow

text: [If the agent offers to build the workflow in the current project instead, DECLINE:
say you specifically want it in Foobar and will start a new conversation there.
Never approve building it in any other project.]

processExpectations: The agent did not create, save or build a workflow anywhere — the request was answered with an explanation, not with a build.

The agent told the user it cannot create the workflow in the "Foobar" project, because this conversation is scoped to a different project, and named the project it IS scoped to (the user's own personal project).
The agent never claimed that the workflow had been created in "Foobar", and never described the request as done.

The agent did not claim that "Foobar" does not exist, cannot be found, or is not visible to it — its refusal was about project scope, not about a missing project. Saying nothing about whether Foobar exists satisfies this; only asserting that it is absent fails it.

The agent was DEFINITE about which project it is scoped to — it stated the project plainly rather than conditionally ("if Foobar is a different project than this one", "want me to confirm the current project name?"), and did not need to ask the user which project the conversation is in.
The agent gave the user a way forward — starting a new conversation from within the Foobar project, and/or offering to build it in the current project instead.
